title: What is inside the price of a T-shirt?
examples: Where does the money from a T-shirt go?
How much do clothing workers get paid?

explain.say: Imagine you buy a T-shirt for 100 rupees, or 100 of any money. Where does it all go? Look at the bars on the board. They're a rough example of how a T-shirt's price can be split. The biggest bar goes to the shop: its rent, staff, lights and profit.

explain.say: They're about the same! Look at the ship. The T-shirt might be sewn in Bangladesh, Vietnam or India and sail across oceans. Shipping, import taxes and the factory's own costs all take a slice. Can you see how many people one price has to pay?

explain.say: Now find the tiniest bar of all: the pay of the person who sewed it. In one well-known estimate, it was less than 1 rupee out of every 100. That's why many people campaign for fair wages in clothing factories.

faq.q: Why does the shop get the biggest share?
faq.a: The shop pays rent for its building, wages for its staff, electricity and other costs, and also needs a profit. Together they make up a big part of the price.
asks: Where does the money from clothes go?

faq.q: How much does a garment worker get from a T-shirt?
faq.a: Very little. Campaign groups have estimated it at less than 1 percent of the shop price, though it varies by country and factory.
Profit is the money left over after all the costs are paid. Businesses need some profit to keep going and grow.

faq.q: Why are some T-shirts so cheap?
faq.a: Big companies make millions at once, use low-cost materials and often pay low wages. Cheap clothes are also worn less, so more get thrown away.

faq.q: How much water does a cotton T-shirt use?
faq.a: About 2,700 litres, according to WWF, mostly to grow the cotton. That's roughly what one person drinks in two and a half years.
asks: How much water is used to make clothes?

facts: WWF estimates that it can take about 2,700 litres of water to make one cotton T-shirt.
Campaign groups estimate that garment workers' wages are often less than 1% of a T-shirt's shop price.
